correctness.rationale: Recomputed the Gaussian radial integrals in the normalized 1,z basis: diagonal entries a(1-e^-t), a(1-(1+t)e^-t), off diagonal c_E=G(t)/(2 pi)*integral_E e^{i theta}. The circle rearrangement bound |integral_E e^{i theta}|<=2 sin(pi a), equality only for a single arc, remains sharp for arbitrary measurable masks. Traceless Hermitian matrices become Bloch vectors (Re c,Im c,h); Pauli commutator has norm twice cross product magnitude. For nonpositive cosine of angle, its squared norm increases with the horizontal radii, so both masks must be arcs. Strict concavity of the residual quadratic in cos delta gives the stated two branches and exact equality. rho_a(t) strictly decreases from infinity to zero by positive integral representation, yielding one radius. Independently recomputed representative Gaussian sector matrices and commutator norm at four parameter sets. No full Fock-space assertion is made.

final_claim: For arbitrary measurable circle masks E,F of fixed measures 2 pi a,2 pi b with a,b in (0,1), disk-clipped at squared radius t>0, the commutator of compressed Toeplitz matrices on span{1,z} has a sharp two-branch norm: 2 sqrt((s_a^2+h_a^2)(s_b^2+h_b^2)) if rho_a rho_b<=1 and 2(h_a s_b+h_b s_a) otherwise; all maximizers are single arcs and their separation changes uniquely from antipodal to an obtuse nonantipodal angle.
